subject: Agriculture
title: Weeds as Parasites
description: A 60-second lesson on Weeds as Parasites.

hook.text: Striga—the witchweed—attaches to crop roots and steals water, nutrients, and sugars. It's invisible above ground.

buildup.text: Striga infests 50 million hectares in Africa, devastating corn, sorghum, and millet—the staple crops of the poorest.

discovery.text: A single Striga plant produces 200,000 seeds that can survive in soil for 20 years, waiting for a host.

twist.text: Striga seeds germinate only when they detect chemicals from a crop root nearby—it hunts its victims chemically.

climax.text: Scientists are developing 'suicidal germination'—tricking Striga seeds to sprout without a host, killing them.

punchline.text: The weed that hunts by smell. The cure: faking the smell.

quiz.question: How does Striga detect host crop roots?
options: By sensing chemical signals from nearby crop roots

details.summary: Weeds compete with crops for light, water, and nutrients, reducing yields by an average of 34% globally when uncontrolled. This topic covers how weeds function as parasites of agricultural systems, the most damaging weed species, and why weed management is the farmers largest ongoing cost.
details.whyItMatters: Weeds are the single largest cause of crop yield loss worldwide, exceeding damage from insects and diseases combined. Effective weed management consumes more farmer time and money than any other pest category.
takeaways: Uncontrolled weeds reduce global crop yields by an estimated 34% on average
Weeds compete for light, water, nutrients, and physical space with crop plants
Some weeds are parasitic, attaching directly to crop roots to steal nutrients

faq.question: How do weeds reduce crop yields so dramatically?
faq.answer: Weeds compete for sunlight by growing above crop canopies, absorb soil water and nutrients before crops can access them, and physically crowd out crop plants. Some parasitic weeds like Striga attach directly to crop roots and steal water and nutrients from within.

faq.question: What are the most economically damaging weeds in global agriculture?
faq.answer: Striga (witchweed) devastates cereal crops across Africa, affecting 50 million hectares. Palmer amaranth threatens U.S. row crops with herbicide resistance. Barnyard grass is a major rice weed in Asia. Cyperus rotundus (nutsedge) is considered the world's worst weed.
